result.title: Minimax-Optimal Predictive Flow Matching under Distribution Drift
result.summary: Flow matching learns a generative velocity field by regression, but under distribution drift a field must be deployed before the current data arrive. We study this predictive problem for a fixed, possibly nonconvex, neural class, with dynamic regret against the best represented field of each round. We propose DyProd-FM, which refits flow matching on dyadic historical prefixes and selects among the fits with a sleeping Prod master. Without knowing any drift budget, it attains regret $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_ω+1,1+\sqrt{TΩ}\})$ in the relative velocity risk variation $Ω$ and $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_μ+1,1+T^{1/3}V_μ^{2/3}\})$ in the target-law variation $V_μ=\sum_t W_2(μ_{t+1},μ_t)$, up to approximation and fitting costs. Matching lower bounds for fixed classes show that both rates are optimal in $T$ and in the budgets up to logarithmic factors. Prior optimal dynamic-regret guarantees rely on a convex decision set with strongly convex or exp-concave losses, whereas our class may be nonconvex and no curvature in its parameters is assumed. The target-law rate rests on a second-order link between the two variations, which the base noise of flow matching provides.

AI.brief_summary: 研究分布漂移下针对固定（可能非凸）神经类别的预测式 flow matching：提出 DyProd-FM，用二进历史前缀重拟合速度场并以 sleeping Prod master 在线选择，在未知漂移预算下给出相对速度风险与目标分布变化两种度量的动态遗憾上界及匹配下界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无需已知漂移预算」的多假设在线加权与动态遗憾上下界分析，可能为 LVR 中多 latent 假设的动态选择、计算分配与停止决策提供可核查的工具性线索，但与视觉推理状态本身无直接关联。
